title: International Scientia Coursework Scholarship
program_type: University merit scholarship requiring a separate application (competitive tuition-fee scholarship, one of several awards under the UNSW Scholarships for Commencing International Students advertisement)
funding_type: Tuition fee remission only (full tuition for the minimum duration of programme, or an annual tuition contribution), university-funded
administering_authority: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
implementing_agency: UNSW Scholarships Office, University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
programme_action: UNSW Scholarships for Commencing International Students (PUCA1029) - Term 1 2027 package
description: The International Scientia Coursework Scholarship (PUCA1025) is the flagship award of UNSW Sydney's international commencing-student scholarship package, advertised under UNSW Scholarships for International Students Commencing Term 1, 2027 (PUCA1029). International students applying for admission to an eligible UNSW undergraduate or postgraduate coursework programme submit one PUCA1029 application and may be considered for PUCA1025 and the other awards in the package. Successful PUCA1025 recipients are offered either full tuition fee support for the minimum duration of the programme, or an annual contribution of AUD $20,000 towards tuition fees for the minimum duration of the programme. Selection is based on academic merit, leadership, extra-curricular activity and the applicant's reasons for studying at UNSW.

award_types: Offer 1: Full tuition fee scholarship paid directly towards tuition fees for the minimum duration of program
Offer 2: AUD $20,000 per annum paid directly towards tuition fees for the minimum duration of program
programme_structure.award_types_detail: Two offer forms of the same scholarship (PUCA1025). Offer 1 is a full tuition fee scholarship; Offer 2 is an annual tuition contribution of AUD $20,000. Both run for the minimum duration of the programme. The PUCA1029 page also lists the wider package: UNSW Law & Justice International Award (PUCA1028) AUD $10,000 for 1 year; UNSW Business School International Pathways Award (PUCA1023) AUD $15,000 for 1 year; UNSW Business School International Scholarship (PUCA1024) AUD $5,000 for the minimum duration of programme; UNSW Hong Kong Foundation Scholarship (UGCA1603) AUD $10,000 per annum for the minimum duration of the program; Dr Vincent Lo Asia Undergraduate Scholarship (UGCA1606) AUD $10,000 per annum for the minimum duration of programme (up to 5 years), restricted to international students from Asia. Awards offered automatically at admission without a separate application are Australia's Global University Award (PUCA1026) AUD $10,000 for 1 year, UNSW College Award (PUCA1027) AUD $10,000 for 1 year, UNSW Masters of Laws Scholarship (PGCA1107) AUD $20,000 for 1 year and the UNSW Articulation Scholarships (UGCA1815, UGCA1817, UGCA1818, UGCA1825) AUD $5,000 p.a. stipend for the minimum duration of programme.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: The award runs for the minimum duration of the programme rather than being re-competed annually. The PUCA1029 FAQs state that in general, to keep the scholarship a recipient must meet the ongoing enrolment and academic requirements and be enrolled in an eligible programme each term, with specifics in the individual offer letter.
programme_structure.intake: Term 1 2027 (international students commencing their first term of study at UNSW)

application_deadline.typical_application_window: Opens 6 July 2026 and closes 30 October 2026 (11:59 AEST) for Term 1 2027 commencement. The PUCA1029 FAQs separately state that Term 1 applications are generally open 1 September - 30 November each year.
application_deadline.application_period: 6 July 2026 to 30 October 2026, 11:59 AEST (for commencement in Term 1 2027)
application_deadline.official_rule: Per the PUCA1029 page: 'Please note this application will open on 06 July 2026 and close at AEST 11:59PM on 30 October 2026.' The site summary metadata for the same page lists Opens 15/07/2026 and Closes 30/10/2026. Applicants must have received an offer of admission into an eligible programme for Term 1 2027 by 30 October 2026. The FAQ document states late applications cannot be accepted and scholarships under PUCA1029 are not deferrable.

Applicants must have received an unconditional offer of admission by 30 October 2026 to be considered eligible, and UNSW advises applicants not to wait for the scholarship outcome before applying to study. UNSW reserves the right not to award a scholarship where there is no applicant of sufficient merit.

programme_duration.official_range: Minimum duration of the programme funded (Offer 1 full tuition; Offer 2 AUD $20,000 per annum). The Dr Vincent Lo Asia Undergraduate Scholarship (UGCA1606) within the same package is capped at up to 5 years.
programme_duration.renewal_note: Coverage runs for the minimum duration of the enrolled programme rather than being re-awarded each year. Recipients must meet ongoing enrolment and academic requirements and remain enrolled in an eligible programme each term (per the PUCA1029 FAQs); the specific conditions are set out in the offer letter. UNSW notes a new flex-semester academic calendar begins in 2028, which may alter the duration of studies for students who commence before 2028.

funding.scholarship_type: Tuition fee contribution scholarship (full tuition or annual tuition contribution)
funding.monthly_amount_note: No stipend or monthly allowance is published for the International Scientia Coursework Scholarship. Contributions are paid directly towards tuition fees each term; no bank details are required for tuition-payment scholarships. Some other awards inside the PUCA1029 package (the UNSW Articulation Scholarships, UGCA1815/UGCA1817/UGCA1818/UGCA1825) are paid as a stipend fortnightly to the recipient's Australian bank account.
funding.travel_amount_note: No travel amount published. UNSW states in the PUCA1029 FAQs that there are no scholarships that will cover the full costs of studying and living in Australia.
funding.fully_funded_note: Offer 1 covers full tuition fees for the minimum duration of the programme but no living costs, travel, visa or insurance. UNSW states explicitly that 'there are no scholarships that will cover the full costs of studying and living in Australia' and advises international students not to rely solely on scholarship support.

tuition.amount: Offer 1: full tuition fee scholarship; Offer 2: AUD $20,000 per annum
tuition.conditions: Paid directly towards tuition fees for the minimum duration of the programme. Payments are made prior to the census date of each term.

monthly_stipend.note: Not published for PUCA1025. The UNSW Articulation Scholarships inside the same PUCA1029 package pay a AUD $5,000 p.a. stipend for the minimum duration of programme.

bond.note: No service bond or repayment obligation is published for PUCA1025

total_estimated_value.note: Not computed. The official source publishes a per-annum or full-tuition benefit rather than a total programme value, and the contract bars presenting a computed total as an award.

eligible_applicants: International students (any country) commencing full-time study in a UNSW undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree programme
Applicants who have received an offer of admission into an eligible Term 1 2027 programme by 30 October 2026
Undergraduate applicants who have completed an assessable Senior Secondary School qualification immediately prior to commencing study at UNSW
Applicants with pending Year 12 (or equivalent) results and UAC International applicants, who may still apply by the deadline
final_year_condition: Applies to completion of the final year of senior secondary / high school, not a prior bachelor's degree. Applicants with pending Year 12 (or equivalent) results and UAC International applicants may still apply by the deadline; however, offers will only be made to successful recipients with an UNSW Letter of Offer (unconditional). UNSW accepts predicted grades for full offers for IB, A-Levels, Indian CBSE, Singapore A-levels, NCUK and South African NSC, and accepts SAT, AP or ACT results for full or conditional-on-English offers ahead of final high school completion.
equivalent_degree_note: UNSW recognises assessable international Senior Secondary School qualifications and their equivalents for undergraduate entry. UNSW now accepts predicted grades for full offers for International Baccalaureate (IB), A-Levels, Indian CBSE, Singapore A-levels, NCUK and South African NSC, with a buffer of 2 points above the standard entry requirement. Students who meet programme entry requirements on SAT, AP or ACT results are eligible for a full or conditional-on-English offer ahead of final high school results and proof of completion. Applicants from International Student Award eligible countries are automatically assessed under the International Admissions Diversity Pathway, which adds 5 points to their International ATAR (minimum International ATAR of 75 required; excludes Bachelor of Medical Studies/Doctor of Medicine).

eligibility.citizenship: Open to international students of any nationality. The parent PUCA1029 advertisement requires applicants to be an international student; there is no nationality restriction on PUCA1025 itself. Other awards inside the same package are country-restricted (UNSW Hong Kong Foundation Scholarship UGCA1603 for citizens of Hong Kong; Dr Vincent Lo Asia Undergraduate Scholarship UGCA1606 for international students from Asia).
eligibility.residence_requirement: No separate residence requirement is published for PUCA1025. The programme must be an on-campus UNSW programme: UNSW Online and UNSW Canberra programmes are excluded. Applicants must not be current UNSW students (this last condition applies to the separate International Student Award).
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Undergraduate applicants must have completed an assessable Senior Secondary School qualification immediately prior to commencing study at UNSW and, for PUCA1024, must not have undertaken prior tertiary study. Applicants with pending Year 12 or equivalent results may still apply by the deadline.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Assessed on academic merit via the application for admission and the scholarship application. No minimum ATAR, International ATAR, GPA or percentage is published for PUCA1025. For reference, UNSW publishes indicative International ATAR entry requirements per programme in its 2027 undergraduate entry requirements table, and the International Admissions Diversity Pathway requires a minimum International ATAR of 75 to add 5 points.
eligibility.language_requirement: English-language conditions on the offer of admission must be resolved: an offer with outstanding English language conditions does not satisfy the PUCA1029 requirement unless it is a Conditional English Package Offer (UEEC), where the student must be enrolled in the UNSW Institute of Languages and successfully complete the programme before commencing in Term 1 2027.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: Extra-curricular activities are one of the four published selection criteria (sporting, cultural activities, volunteer or work experience) and must be evidenced with supporting documents.
eligibility.leadership_requirement: Leadership skills demonstrated at school, in the workplace or in the community are one of the four published selection criteria and must be evidenced.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: Applicants may not hold more than one international scholarship at any given time; the only exception is the International Student Award. A full tuition fee scholarship may not be held together with the International Student Award.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Must be a commencing international student, i.e. starting their first term of study at UNSW in Term 1 2027, enrolled full-time in an eligible programme.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: No fixed percentage, ATAR or GPA threshold is published for the International Scientia Coursework Scholarship. Academic merit is assessed through the UNSW admission application together with the scholarship application.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: Programme-specific rules apply to other awards in the package: the UNSW Business School International Scholarship (PUCA1024) requires undergraduate applicants to have completed an assessable Senior Secondary School qualification immediately prior to commencing study at UNSW and not to have undertaken prior tertiary study, and bars recipients of the UNSW Business School International Pathways Award (PUCA1023). The UNSW Business School International Pathways Award (PUCA1023) additionally requires an undergraduate articulation pathway qualification from an approved partner institution or completion of UNSW Foundation Studies Commerce or Commerce Actuarial stream. The UNSW Law & Justice International Award (PUCA1028) is limited to LLB, JD or LLM programmes.
selection_factors_may_include: Extra-curricular activities (sporting, cultural activities, volunteer or work experience)
Reasons for undertaking studies at UNSW
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: UNSW states its scholarships are not solely based on grades: leadership skills, extracurricular interests and ambition to make a positive impact are also valued. Every claim made in the application must be supported by documentation; unanswered application questions or claims without supporting documentation will not be assessed.

english_requirement.test_score_note: No English test scores are published on the scholarship page. English proficiency is an admission requirement assessed by UNSW Admissions: a conditional offer whose only outstanding condition is an English language requirement does not satisfy the PUCA1029 offer requirement, unless it is a Conditional English Package Offer (UEEC) under which the student is enrolled in the UNSW Institute of Languages and successfully completes the programme before commencing in Term 1 2027. Minimum scores for individual programmes are published by UNSW separately on the English language requirements pages and were not verified for this record.

language_of_instruction.language_note: All eligible UNSW coursework programmes are taught in English. UNSW College UEEC is offered as a packaged English pathway for applicants who do not already meet the English language requirement.

application_method.application_route: Register an account in the UNSW Scholarship Application Online portal and submit the PUCA1029 application (UNSW Scholarships for International Students Commencing Term 1, 2027), which considers the applicant for the International Scientia Coursework Scholarship (PUCA1025) and the other listed awards.
application_steps: Apply for admission to an eligible UNSW undergraduate or postgraduate coursework programme through the UNSW Applicant Portal (apply.unsw.edu.au) or, for UAC International applicants, through UAC.

Receive an offer of admission (unconditional Letter of Offer, or a conditional Letter of Offer whose outstanding conditions do not include Genuine Student or English language requirements, or a Conditional English Package Offer (UEEC)) by 30 October 2026.

Register an account in the UNSW Scholarship Application Online portal at https://scholarships.online.unsw.edu.au/scholarship/sc_search.login (register as a 'future student' if no offer has yet been received).

Complete and submit the PUCA1029 application before 11:59 AEST on 30 October 2026, including all written responses and evidence supporting claims of academic achievement, leadership and extra-curricular activity.
Combine all supporting documents into a single PDF of no more than 10 MB, in English, and upload it to the application.

After the closing date, track the application status in the portal (statuses include Being assessed, Shortlisted for consideration, Wait Reserve, Successful Conditional Offer, Unsuccessful, Selected) and accept the scholarship offer letter before its lapse date if successful.

selection_process.decision_maker: UNSW Scholarships Office with a UNSW panel (UNSW Sydney)
selection_process.selection_type: Competitive application-based, assessed against published selection criteria
possible_stages: Application submitted through the Scholarship Application Online portal by 30 October 2026
Eligibility checking by the UNSW Scholarships team
Scoring of each eligible application by the panel
Scores tallied by the Scholarships team to identify successful recipients for each scholarship
Notification by email to view the scholarship offer letter in the scholarships system
Acceptance of the offer before its lapse date; ongoing enrolment and academic requirements apply thereafter
selection_process.weighting_note: UNSW publishes no numerical weighting for the four selection criteria. The FAQs describe panel scoring of eligible applications followed by tallying to determine the final ranking; scholarships are highly competitive and fewer scholarships are available than applicants.
selection_process.results_timing: The UNSW Scholarships Office endeavours to respond within 30 days after the closing date of application, though it may occasionally take longer. Outcomes are visible in the scholarship login page as Being assessed, Shortlisted for consideration, Wait Reserve, Successful Conditional Offer, Unsuccessful or Selected.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: Final ranking is determined by the UNSW panel. The number of PUCA1029 scholarships awarded each term is not disclosed; it depends on the competitiveness of the applicant pool, the scholarship budget and panel decisions.

additional_factors: Reasons for undertaking studies at UNSW

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: The eligible UNSW coursework degree the recipient is admitted to (bachelor degree at undergraduate level); the scholarship is not itself a qualification
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: Minimum duration of the enrolled programme (Australian bachelor's degrees are typically 3 to 4 years full-time; the source does not publish a single figure)
possible_awards: Offer 1: full tuition fee scholarship for the minimum duration of programme
Offer 2: AUD $20,000 per annum towards tuition fees for the minimum duration of programme
Possible guaranteed entry to the UNSW Professional Development Program
degree_outcome.degree_note: Eligible programmes are undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree programmes, excluding UNSW Online and UNSW Canberra. UNSW is introducing a new flex-semester academic calendar from 2028; while degree structure and requirements remain the same, the duration of studies may vary depending on when a student commences prior to 2028.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Full tuition fees are paid for the minimum duration of the programme (Offer 1), or AUD $20,000 per annum is contributed towards tuition fees (Offer 2). Contributions are paid directly to the fee account each term, prior to the census date; no bank details are required for tuition-payment scholarships.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: UNSW Scholarships does not charge a scholarship application or processing fee, and warns that any request for such a fee is a cyber scam that should be reported to scholarships@unsw.edu.au. (Any separate UNSW admission application fee is set by UNSW Admissions and is not waived by this scholarship.)
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: Recipients accept a scholarship offer letter that sets out the terms and conditions of the scholarship, including ongoing enrolment and academic requirements.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: Scholarship recipients may be offered guaranteed entry to the UNSW Professional Development Program. General support services are described on unsw.edu.au/study/discover/student-support.

Whether a separate application is required (PUCA1025 requires one; the International Student Award PUCA1030, Australia's Global University Award PUCA1026 and UNSW College Award PUCA1027 do not)

practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: For PUCA1025, the written responses should directly address the four published selection criteria: academic merit, leadership (school, workplace or community), extra-curricular activities (sporting, cultural, volunteer or work experience) and the applicant's reasons for undertaking studies at UNSW. Make each claim specific, name the role or activity, the year and the outcome, and attach the matching document. Because unlisted evidence is subject to approval, contact the scholarships office if unsure. For the separate 20% International Student Award, the required document is a personal statement of no more than 500 words outlining reasons for studying the proposed programme at UNSW, assessed on academic merit plus aptitude and commitment to studies.

School leaver entering directly from senior secondary school

Making claims in the application without uploading supporting documentation, which are then not assessed
Uploading multiple files instead of one merged PDF, or exceeding the 10 MB limit
Uploading documents that are not in English, are not translated by a translation organisation, or are more than three years old
Assuming the award can be deferred; scholarships under PUCA1029 are not deferrable and are rescinded if the recipient cannot commence in the term
Assuming the 20% International Student Award can be stacked on a full tuition scholarship
Assuming the scholarship covers living costs; UNSW states no scholarship covers the full costs of studying and living in Australia

risk_flags.risk: Scholarships are highly competitive and fewer scholarships are available than applicants
risk_flags.impact: High - most applicants will not receive PUCA1025, and UNSW advises international students not to rely solely on scholarship support
risk_flags.mitigation: Apply broadly, secure an unconditional admission offer early, evidence every claim, and budget for full tuition and living costs as the default scenario

risk_flags.risk: An unconditional offer of admission must be held by 30 October 2026
risk_flags.impact: High - a pending or ineligible conditional offer disqualifies an otherwise strong application
risk_flags.mitigation: Lodge the admission application months earlier and confirm offer type; note that conditional offers are acceptable only when the outstanding conditions exclude Genuine Student and English language requirements (or are a UEEC package)

risk_flags.risk: Claims in the application are only assessed if supported by documentation
risk_flags.impact: High - unevidenced claims score nothing, materially reducing an application
risk_flags.mitigation: Build the supporting PDF alongside the application, keep documents within three years and in English, and contact scholarships@unsw.edu.au at least one week before closing

risk_flags.risk: Scholarships under PUCA1029 are not deferrable
risk_flags.impact: Medium - a delayed visa or deferred offer causes the scholarship to be rescinded at the commencement of term
risk_flags.mitigation: Apply for the student visa as soon as the Confirmation of Enrolment is received and do not plan a deferred commencement alongside the scholarship

risk_flags.risk: Only one international scholarship may be held at a time, and a full tuition scholarship cannot be combined with the 20% International Student Award
risk_flags.impact: Medium - the total benefit may be smaller than expected
risk_flags.mitigation: Read the specific offer letter and compare the actual net benefit before accepting; the International Student Award can be combined with non-full-tuition scholarships

risk_flags.risk: UNSW is moving to a flex-semester academic calendar from 2028
risk_flags.impact: Low to medium - programme duration, and therefore the length of a 'minimum duration' award, may change
risk_flags.mitigation: Confirm the current academic calendar and programme duration with UNSW before accepting the offer

risk_flags.risk: Cyber scams requesting a scholarship application or processing fee
risk_flags.impact: Financial loss if a fake fee is paid
risk_flags.mitigation: UNSW Scholarships does not charge an application or processing fee; report any such request to scholarships@unsw.edu.au and do not pay

risk_flags.risk: UNSW reserves the right not to award a scholarship where there is no applicant of sufficient merit
risk_flags.impact: Low - awards may not be filled at all
risk_flags.mitigation: Treat the funding as contingent until the offer letter is received and accepted

database_notes: This record is for the International Scientia Coursework Scholarship (PUCA1025), the flagship award of the UNSW Scholarships for International Students Commencing Term 1, 2027 (PUCA1029) package, researched on 2026-10-03. It funds a bachelor's degree, so degree = Bachelor's and bachelor_requirement = true (it funds a bachelor's programme).

Substitution: none required. The target was not excluded - PUCA1025/PUCA1029 does not appear in the RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.md do-not-duplicate list, whose only Australia entries are Melbourne International Undergraduate Scholarship, UTS Vice-Chancellor's International Undergraduate Scholarship and VUW Undergraduate International Scholarship. The same original filename was used.

Opening-date discrepancy: the body text of the PUCA1029 page states the application 'will open on 06 July 2026 and close at AEST 11:59PM on 30 October 2026', while the same page's summary metadata lists Opens 15/07/2026 and Closes 30/10/2026. The closing date is unambiguous (30 October 2026) and is recorded as the exact deadline; the opening date is recorded as 6 July 2026 per the body text, with the 15 July 2026 figure noted here. No other date was inferred.

Window discrepancy: the PUCA1029 FAQs state that Term 1 applications are generally open 1 September - 30 November, whereas the Term 1 2027 page states 6 July - 30 October 2026. Both are recorded; the cycle-specific figures on the Term 1 2027 advertisement were treated as authoritative for this cycle.
No official acronym or short form exists for PUCA1025; short_title is a descriptive short form, not an official one.

legacy_titles is empty because the official pages publish no alternative names for this award. 'UNSW Scholarships for International Students Commencing Term 1, 2027 (PUCA1029)' is the name of the parent advertisement/application, not a legacy title of the award, and is recorded in programme_structure.

funding.fully_funded is set to false: Offer 1 covers tuition only, and UNSW explicitly states there are no scholarships that cover the full costs of studying and living in Australia. The award is presented as tuition-fee support, not as a fully funded place.
No bond or repayment obligation is published for PUCA1025, so bond_requirement is false and bond_breach_consequence is null.

english_requirement.universal_requirement is false because the scholarship page itself publishes no English test requirement; English proficiency is an admission condition assessed by UNSW Admissions, and conditional offers with outstanding English conditions do not satisfy the PUCA1029 offer requirement unless they are a UEEC package.
No interview is mentioned in the official material, so interview_required and interview_possible are false; these are absences of evidence rather than explicit denials.
The number of PUCA1029 scholarships awarded each term is not disclosed by UNSW (depends on the applicant pool, budget and panel decisions), so no award count is recorded.

Other awards in the same PUCA1029 package are described in programme_structure.award_types_detail and in verification.official_fields_confirmed rather than as separate records, because the assignment is one record for this slot and they share a single application form.

The separate 20% International Student Award (PUCA1030) is described where relevant because it forms part of the wider UNSW international undergraduate scholarship package, but it is a distinct award with its own eligibility country list and its own 500-word personal statement.

A new flex-semester academic calendar is being introduced by UNSW from 2028; degree structure and requirements remain unchanged but programme duration may vary for students who commence before 2028. This affects the interpretation of 'minimum duration of programme'.

Holding restriction (recorded under eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction and coverage_limitations, not as a separate top-level key): the PUCA1029 FAQs state that applicants may not hold more than one international scholarship at any given time, the only exception being the International Student Award, and that a full tuition fee scholarship may not be held together with the International Student Award. This is a holding restriction rather than a bar on re-applying to PUCA1025 in a future cycle, so no top-level previous_award_restriction key was added.

Admission versus funding (hard accuracy rule 3): the International Scientia Coursework Scholarship (PUCA1025) is NOT automatic - it requires a separate application through the Scholarship Application Online portal, and programme_structure records application_required = true and automatic_consideration = false. Within the same PUCA1029 package, Australia's Global University Award (PUCA1026), UNSW College Award (PUCA1027), UNSW Masters of Laws Scholarship (PGCA1107) and the UNSW Articulation Scholarships (UGCA1815, UGCA1817, UGCA1818, UGCA1825) ARE automatic: eligible students who have received an offer of admission are considered without submitting any scholarship application or additional documentation, assessed on academic merit only. The 20% International Student Award (PUCA1030) sits between the two: eligible students are considered for it when applying for admission to UNSW and, if eligible, are invited to submit a brief statement of no more than 500 words about their motivation to study at UNSW, uploaded through the UNSW Applicant Portal or myUNSW; it is assessed on academic merit plus aptitude and commitment to studies, and confirmation is emailed within two days of receiving the offer (or within two weeks of uploading the statement for existing offer holders).
